topPRs.title: feat(monetization): debit org credit balance + rebuild app-auth consent flow
topPRs.author: NubsCarson
topPRs.body:
> Re-opened from #473 after a branch-rename closed the original. Same commits, same content.

## TL;DR

Two intertwined cleanups for the app-monetization story plus the OAuth consent flow:

1. **Reworks `appCreditsService`** so monetized apps debit the **user's organization credit balance** instead of the per-app `app_credit_balances` pool. Any signed-in cloud user can use any monetized app without first topping up a per-app pot. Creator markup share + redeemable_earnings flow still fires through `recordCreatorEarnings()`.
2. **Rebuilds `/app-auth/authorize`** UX. Old code auto-redirected on `isAuthenticated` and bailed silently when `useAuth().user` hadn't hydrated, which left users staring at a Cancel-only screen. New flow shows an explicit **"Authorize <App>"** button and a checkmark "Signed in" status. Standard OAuth consent UX, no silent failure modes.

Plus the smaller fixes that fell out of testing:

- COOP `same-origin-allow-popups` on `/app-auth/*` so OAuth popups can call `window.closed` without throwing.
- Connect-src CSP allows `localhost:3200` when `NEXT_PUBLIC_STEWARD_AUTH_ENABLED=true` (so a local Steward dev server is reachable from a browser running against `next start`).
- Drop `LandingHeader` from the consent screen — its server/client auth-state mismatch ("Log in" vs "Dashboard") was throwing a hydration error that remounted the React tree mid-flight and prevented `validateApp`'s effect from completing.
- Drop the dead `<video src="/videos/Hero...mp4">` element (asset isn't checked in; was 404'ing in 60s+ on every page load).
- Truncate the user-menu dropdown email so long addresses stop overflowing the `w-56` container.

## Why this matters

The org-balance rework is the load-bearing piece. Before this PR a user had to discover **per-app credits** as a separate concept, top up each app individually, and the in-app deduct path went through a different service from the rest of cloud's billing. After this PR, the marketplace promise is honest: **one balance, any monetized app, creator + affiliate still earn their cut.**

## What's verified

End-to-end against a local cloud-fork + Steward + agent-home eDad reference app:

\`\`\`
ORG balance:      999.999147 → 999.999467     (debited \$0.000277 = base + 100% markup)
APP pool:         100.04     → 100.04          (untouched ✅ — no per-app deduction)
CREATOR earnings: 0.000000   → 0.000229       (creator markup share)
PLATFORM revenue: 0.000000   → 0.000229       (base cost)
REDEEMABLE_EARNINGS: 0       → 0.0002         (creator's withdrawable balance)
\`\`\`

New-user JIT sync also exercised: brand-new Steward JWT → `syncUserFromSteward` provisions cloud user + org with $5 welcome credit → chat charges $0.000588 → creator earnings tick up. Same pattern as existing user.

## Migration notes for redeploy

- **No DB migration**. The existing `app_credit_balances` table is left in place — no data loss, just no longer the deduction target. Per-app pools you've sold remain readable; new chats just don't decrement them.
- **No env changes required.** All existing config still works.
- **App-creator UI changes** (the per-app credit pool view in the dashboard) may now show stale values vs. activity. Worth a follow-up to repurpose that view as "earnings from this app" instead.
- **Pricing math** is unchanged: `baseCost * (1 + inference_markup_percentage / 100)` debited atomically from `organizations.credit_balance` via `creditsService.reserveAndDeductCredits` (same row-lock pattern used by every other org-balance debit in cloud).

## Code-quality notes

- Audited per the 5-rule no-slop pass: dropped redundant intermediate variables, inlined single-call helpers, removed defensive fallbacks for cases that can't happen.
- All new auth-page components are local to `authorize-content.tsx` (Frame, AppHeader, PermissionsList, SignedInActions, SignedOutActions) — no new shared abstractions.

## File-by-file

- `packages/lib/services/app-credits.ts` — checkBalance / deductCredits / reconcileCredits all reach into `organizations.credit_balance` via `creditsService`. Refund path uses `refundCredits`.
- `app/api/v1/messages/route.ts` — for the app-credits flow, `estimatedBaseCost` is now `0` so reconcile charges the full actual cost as the diff (the anonymous reservation never debited upfront).
- `packages/ui/src/components/auth/authorize-content.tsx` — full rewrite of the consent screen.
- `packages/ui/src/components/layout/user-menu.tsx` — `truncate` + `min-w-0` + `title=...` on the email row.
- `next.config.ts` — COOP for `/app-auth/*`, CSP gate for local Steward.

## What I want maintainer eyes on

1. The org-balance debit semantics in `reconcileCredits` — I assume the messages-route flow is the only caller that uses `estimatedBaseCost: 0`. If anything else still passes a real estimate, the "diff" math will under-charge.
2. Whether the per-app credit pool concept should be **removed** entirely (deprecate `app_credit_balances` table, drop the dashboard UI for it, drop `processPurchase` for app credits) in a follow-up. This PR keeps it readable but inert.
3. The `force-dynamic` page `/app-auth/authorize` is heavier in dev-mode webpack compile after this rewrite (it pulls `<StewardLogin>` from `@stwd/react`) — if Vercel cold-starts feel slow, consider `generateStaticParams` or splitting StewardLogin to client-only chunk.

## Test plan
- [ ] Sign in to https://app.elizacloud.ai/app-auth/authorize via passkey/email/OAuth — should reach explicit "Authorize <App>" + Cancel
- [ ] Click Authorize — redirect back to app's redirect_uri with token+state
- [ ] Send a message via a monetized app — confirm `organizations.credit_balance` decrements by base*(1+markup)
- [ ] Confirm `apps.total_creator_earnings` and the creator's `redeemable_earnings` rise by base*markup
- [ ] Confirm an unrelated user's `app_credit_balances` row for the same app stays untouched

topPRs.title: feat(billing): pay-as-you-go container hosting from app earnings (with optional toggle)
topPRs.author: NubsCarson
topPRs.body:
Closes the self-hosting loop for monetized apps deployed on Eliza Cloud
containers. When the daily container-billing cron fires, hosting bills
are paid from the org owner's `redeemable_earnings` BEFORE falling
through to `credit_balance`. Apps that earn enough cover their hosting
without ever touching cash credits. Default-on, opt-out at
`/dashboard/billing`.

## The loop this closes

```
user chats with monetized app
    │
    ▼
cloud charges user's org credits + your inference markup %
    │
    ▼
markup credits your redeemable_earnings (existing flow)
    │
    ▼
container daily-billing pulls earnings first, credits second
    │
    ▼
your container stays alive while profitable
```

If the toggle is off, hosting bills come purely from credits and
earnings stay untouched for token cashout. The toggle is on by default
because that's the experience this PR was designed around — opt-out
matches the "pay-as-you-go is the natural state for a monetized app"
framing.

## Verified end-to-end

- ✅ `$5` earnings + `$5` credits, `$0.67` daily bill, **toggle on**:
  earnings → `$4.33`, credits unchanged
- ✅ Same setup, **toggle off**: earnings → `$5` (unchanged), credits → `$4.33`
- ✅ Ledger row + `credit_transactions` row both written each cycle, with
  `paid_from_earnings` + `paid_from_credits` in metadata so invoices
  show the split
- ✅ 160/160 integration tests pass (services suite, real Postgres)
- ✅ `check-types` clean for all touched files
- ✅ All 8 dashboard pages compile (apps, app detail tabs, billing,
  earnings, containers, container detail, analytics)

## What's in here

5 commits, each independently reviewable:

1. `feat(billing)` — backend: 4 migrations, schemas, services
   (`convertToCredits`), container-billing route, billing/settings
   API, redemptions/balance API, integration tests
2. `feat(ui)` — `AutoTopUpCard`, `NumericField`, `PayAsYouGoCard`,
   "Spent on hosting" line on earnings page, `SelfHostCTA` on app
   monetization tab, container detail badge cleanup, sidebar entries
3. `feat(apps)` — apps list rebuilt clean (no Vercel), broken Build
   tab dropped, `CreateAppDialog` cut from 651 → 281 lines (only
   name + URL required), API key reveal gets a clarifying note
4. `fix(auth)` — `use-session-auth` Privy bypass for Steward-only
   setups (was leaving the dashboard spinner stuck), authorize page
   merge resolution dropping a 404'ing video tag + hydration-prone
   header, CSP widened for local Steward
5. `docs` — `docs/building-a-monetized-app.md` (creator recipe) +
   `docs/agent-skill-build-monetized-app.md` (skill spec for the
   Milady/ElizaOS framework agent — survival-game framing)

## Schema changes

Four migrations, each small + focused per `CLAUDE.md` rules:

- `0070` — earnings auto-fund settings columns + `total_converted_to_credits`
- `0071` — `credit_conversion` ledger entry type (separate so the new
  enum value commits before any insert that uses it)
- `0072` — drops the auto-fund columns; replaced with always-on
  pay-as-you-go in container-billing
- `0073` — `pay_as_you_go_from_earnings` boolean (default true)

## Companion PR

The canonical reference implementation that uses this monetization
loop is
[**`elizaOS/cloud-mini-apps#4`**](https://github.com/elizaOS/cloud-mini-apps/pull/4)
(edad-chat). That PR demonstrates:

- Forwarding chats with `x-app-id` + `x-affiliate-code` headers via
  `@elizaos/cloud-sdk`
- Standalone Bun container target (Dockerfile + `server.ts` using the
  SDK)
- The README walkthrough creators copy-paste

Both PRs ship together — without this one, the cloud-mini-apps PR has
nowhere to deposit earnings.

## Open questions / things to discuss

1. **Toggle default — on or off?** Currently default-on (every existing
   org gets pay-as-you-go automatically when this lands). Default-off
   would be more conservative but creates a "this feature does nothing
   until you opt in" UX. The Discord conversation around this favored
   "make it optional" — opting interpretation as "have a toggle"
   rather than "force opt-in". Open to feedback.
2. **`/dashboard/apps/[id]/?tab=domains`** still shows `cname.vercel-dns.com`
   and `76.76.21.21` as the DNS targets. Container deployments use AWS
   ECS load balancers, not Vercel — this is a pre-existing bug,
   unrelated to this PR but worth flagging. Out of scope here; happy
   to fix separately.
3. **`/dashboard/apps/create`** is stubbed to a redirect for now; the
   3,750-line vercel-coupled codebuilder it used to host was disabled
   in `8616f45528` because it couldn't ship cleanly. Original code
   preserved in git history at `ce75ff971d^`. If/when the codebuilder
   gets rebuilt on the container path, a proper page goes back here.
4. **Privy console errors** — `use-session-auth` now ignores Privy's
   never-resolving `ready` flag when Steward is on, which unblocks
   the dashboard. The Privy SDK still floods console with
   "Invalid Privy app ID" on placeholder env vars. Cosmetic only;
   real fix is wrapping `<PrivyProvider>` conditional on Steward —
   out of scope for this PR but happy to follow up.
5. **Agent skill is plan-only.** `docs/agent-skill-build-monetized-app.md`
   spells out the recipe (6 SDK calls, the survival framing, failure
   modes) but the actual skill — Eliza plugin / Claude Code SKILL.md /
   wherever it lives — is next work. PR scope was the platform
   surface; the skill itself is downstream.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test packages/tests/integration/services/` — green
- [x] `bun run db:migrate` against fresh DB — clean
- [x] `bun run check-types` filtered to touched files — empty
- [x] Live container-billing cron triggered 4× during dev with
      various credit/earnings/toggle states — all math correct
- [ ] **Reviewer:** sanity-check the "earnings auto-fund cron" was
      fully demolished (commit `cfcd229fe` in branch history). The
      `e1721a253` commit that introduced it isn't squashed in here —
      the squashed commit is the END state (pay-as-you-go in
      container-billing) but the iteration history on
      `feat/org-balance-monetization-and-app-auth-rebuild` shows the
      journey if curious.
- [ ] **Reviewer:** confirm default-on is correct vs default-off
